question: Will the official result of the Lamag by-election (Sabah), scheduled for January 24, 2026, be overturned before May 1, 2026?
summary: Baseline ensemble assigns a 2% probability of overturning the Lamag by-election result before May 1, 2026.

Adversarial objections identify non-negligible risk factors (independent petition threat, Sabah petition activity) that could raise overturn odds, but they presuppose non-implausible scenarios with high evidentiary thresholds.
The Lamag result featured a large margin (5,681) and a winner sworn in by February 2026, which historically reduces overturn probability.
Taking into account both risk factors and historical context, the calibrated probability is modestly increased to about 4%, with a plausible range roughly 2–8%.

justification.critique_assessment: Objections identify credible, non-implausible risk factors that could raise overturn odds, but they do not imply a high probability given the large victory margin and historical rarity of overturns.
justification.adjustment: Adjusted upward from 0.02 to 0.04 to reflect non-implausible upside risk from petitions and scrutiny, while preserving a low overall probability due to high evidentiary thresholds and prior outcomes.

causal-factors.name: Lamag margin (BN majority 5,681 at by-election)
causal-factors.rationale: A large majority in Lamag reduces the likelihood that an overturn petition succeeds, as petitions tend to target tight races requiring substantial irregularities to overturn results. ([dailyexpress.com.my](https://www.dailyexpress.com.my/news/274624/bn-retains-kinabatangan-lamag-in-by-elections/?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Absence of credible overturn petitions against Lamag as of May 1, 2026
causal-factors.rationale: Public reporting around the Lamag result shows no credible petitions overturning the outcome by the target date, aligning with the overall rarity of successful overturns in Malaysia. ([dailyexpress.com.my](https://www.dailyexpress.com.my/news/274624/bn-retains-kinabatangan-lamag-in-by-elections/?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Historical rarity of overturns in Malaysian elections (Kimanis 2019, Cameron Highlands 2018)
causal-factors.rationale: High-profile overturns are exceptional cases (only a few out of many petitions), indicating a very low base rate for reversals in general elections and by-elections. ([malaymail.com](https://www.malaymail.com/news/malaysia/2019/12/02/ec-to-abide-by-federal-courts-decision-on-kimanis-seat/1815366?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Sabah unity government context and BN strength in by-elections
causal-factors.rationale: The Lamag by-election occurred within a unified Sabah government with BN strength, which historically correlates with lower overturn risk in by-elections. ([thestar.com.my](https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2026/01/25/kinabatangan-lamag-wins-testament-to-unity-govts-strength-says-gagasan-veep?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Legal thresholds and proof requirements for overturns (need clear irregularities like vote-buying)
causal-factors.rationale: Overturn petitions require strong, proven irregularities; the Cameron Highlands and Kimanis precedents illustrate a high evidentiary bar that reduces overturn likelihood. causal-factors.name: Independent petition threat and recount claims in Lamag by-election
causal-factors.rationale: An independent candidate publicly pledged to file an election petition alleging irregularities; such petitions can trigger investigations that challenge results.

causal-factors.name: Historical rarity of overturns in Malaysian elections
causal-factors.rationale: Overturns are exceptional in Malaysia, with only a few notable cases (e.g., Kimanis 2019, Cameron Highlands 2018), suggesting a low base rate.

causal-factors.name: Large Lamag by-election majority for BN
causal-factors.rationale: BN won Lamag by a wide margin (7,269 to 1,588; majority 5,681), reducing the statistical plausibility of overturn.

causal-factors.name: Broad Sabah petition activity and multiple by-elections
causal-factors.rationale: Reports of petitions following Sabah polls and up to five potential by-elections create a conducive environment for legal challenges.

causal-factors.name: Election watchdogs and anti-corruption monitoring intensify scrutiny
causal-factors.rationale: MACC opened a 24-hour operation room for Sabah by-elections to handle misconduct reports, increasing the likelihood that issues could be brought before the courts.

causal-factors.name: Court timelines and lack of overturned Lamag results by May 1, 2026
causal-factors.rationale: Even if petitions are filed, the typical court timelines and absence of known overturns in Lamag by May 1, 2026 argue against a near-term overturn.

causal-factors.name: Large margin of Lamag victory (5,681 votes)
causal-factors.rationale: BN won Lamag by a margin of 5,681 votes, a large margin that lowers the likelihood of reversal via an election petition. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Lamag_by-election?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Active petition efforts surrounding Lamag
causal-factors.rationale: An independent candidate signaled intent to file a petition over Lamag's result, and Sabah election petitions were being pursued around the 2025 polls, which could raise overturn risk modestly. ([thestar.com.my](https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2025/11/30/independent-candidate-to-file-petition-over-lamag-result?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Historical rarity of overturns in Malaysian election petitions
causal-factors.rationale: Notable overturned results exist but are historically rare (e.g., Kimanis 2019 and Cameron Highlands 2018), implying a low base rate for Lamag. ([malaysiakini.com](https://www.malaysiakini.com/news/502068?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Result already validated and sworn in (Feb 2026)
causal-factors.rationale: The Lamag result was formally won by BN and the winner sworn in on February 10, 2026, reducing the likelihood of a later reversal. ([malaymail.com](https://www.malaymail.com/news/malaysia/2019/12/02/ec-to-abide-by-federal-courts-decision-on-kimanis-seat/1815366?utm_source=openai))

synthesis: The baseline probability is very low, and while petitions and scrutiny in Sabah create some upside risk, the large margin and rarity of overturns keep the chance small. The calibrated estimate remains modest, reflecting both the risk signals and historical constraints.
